target_customer: SMEs and businesses paying suppliers or receiving money across borders, especially into and out of Africa and other emerging markets
problem: Businesses pay high bank FX fees and wait long for cross-border settlement, with little liquidity in emerging market currencies.
business_model: FX and payments marketplace taking spread and fees, with business accounts and an API
product_category: Cross-border B2B payments and FX marketplace

founders.name: Ola Oyetayo
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2021 names him CEO; no background found in opened sources

founders.name: Anthony Oduwole
founders.background_notes: Background from the YC company page; CTO title from TechCrunch 2021 (CB Insights lists a different title)

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace, multi-currency accounts and bank and liquidity integrations are standard fintech engineering, with hard parts in compliance and settlement partners.

defensibility.rationale: Payment licences, bank partnerships and liquidity relationships in African corridors are slow to replicate, but the front end is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch 2021 names only traditional banks as the alternative; no incumbent copied or bought it by 2021.

market_need_then: Nigerian-British founders said they saw paying suppliers abroad was slow and costly for emerging market businesses (TechRound interview, secondary account).

branding.domain_note: Originally vertofx.com; vertofx.com now redirects (301) to verto.co, date of switch not found
branding.brand_signature: Founding story of a poker game conversation told in founder interviews

rebrands.why: Shortened name and domain; the reason and date are not stated in sources seen

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence of merch or fan community found

brand_strength.rationale: Trade and African tech press coverage, but no sourced brand pull; the FX suffix was dropped later.

outcome_analysis: Verto raised a 2 million dollar seed in 2019 and a 10 million dollar Series A led by Quona Capital in September 2021, bought the software studio Locusnine in 2022, and kept expanding corridors, reaching 170 staff per the YC listing. It remains active; no Series B or distress was found, and the founders' banking background in African corridors appears to have helped.
notes: Company site vertofx.com redirects to verto.co; redirect was not followed. Founding year is 2018 per YC page and TechCrunch while some sources say 2017. Series A confirmed by TechCrunch and IBS Intelligence and other outlets; seed amount and date from the TechCrunch 2021 article and a linked July 2019 piece (some outlets say 2.1M). Later funding not found in a search for Series B. Competitor list is empty: searches returned only recent landscape pages, nothing dated near 2019.
